newsitem.title: USA: Advanced Technology Labs wins approval.
newsitem.headline: Advanced Technology Labs wins approval.

text.p: Advanced Technology Laboratories Inc said Monday it won federal approval to market its HDI 3000 ultrasound system for breast-tumor imaging.

The company, also known as ATL, said the U.S. Food and Drug Administration granted supplemental pre-market approval for the product. Last April, the agency granted similar authority for an earlier generation of the machine.
The company said the FDA's action was based on an international study that found ATL's devices in conjunction with mammography can reduce the number of breast biopsies needed by 40 percent.
More than 700,000 women undergo breast biopsy annually in the United States alone, but 80 percent of the lumps are found to be benign, the company said.
Ultrasound, while not appropriate in every case, is less invasive and less expensive, according to ATL.
The HDI and HDI 3000 systems are used to provide diagnostic information on a variety of conditions from heart disease to pregnancy.
